summary: Set up HTTPS on node1:8443 via nginx with certificates auto-renewed by a cron-driven script before expiry, and confirmed nginx picks up each renewed certificate via a graceful reload with zero downtime. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol on node1 with verified boot-identity change and full post-restart recovery, including a live cron-triggered renewal after reboot.
actions_performed: Installed nginx and cronie on node1 (RHEL 9)
Created a self-signed root CA at /etc/pki/rotation-ca (10-year validity)

Wrote /usr/local/bin/renew-cert.sh: checks server cert expiry via openssl x509 -checkend 180, issues a fresh CA-signed cert (5 min validity, SANs for node1/NODE_IP/loopback) when within 180s of expiry, atomically replaces key/cert, restores SELinux cert_t context, and gracefully reloads nginx (nginx -s reload) only after nginx -t passes
Fixed an SELinux mislabeling issue via semanage fcontext + restorecon for /etc/pki/rotation-cert and /etc/pki/rotation-ca
Fixed a cron PATH bug: cron's minimal PATH (/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin) omitted /usr/sbin, silently breaking restorecon and nginx reload under cron; switched to absolute paths for both
Deployed nginx server block listening on 0.0.0.0:8443 and [::]:8443 with ssl_certificate/ssl_certificate_key pointing at the rotated cert/key paths
Installed /etc/cron.d/renew-cert running the renewal script every minute via crond
Enabled and started nginx and crond as persistent systemd services
Observed a full automatic renewal cycle live: cert serial rotated (...CF4D -> ...CF4E) exactly at the cron-triggered reload while continuously polling HTTPS every second with zero non-200 responses
Captured pre-restart baseline on node1: boot_id, uptime -s, service states, cert dates/serial, HTTPS 200
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (acknowledgement returned before disconnect), polled until exec was available again
Verified changed boot_id and new uptime -s timestamp on node1 post-restart, proving a genuine reboot

Verified post-restart recovery: nginx and crond active, cert files retained correct SELinux labels, HTTPS answering 200, and a fresh cron-triggered renewal (...CF4E -> ...CF4F) fired on schedule after reboot with zero downtime observed throughout
Cleaned up temporary watch/log files on node1

evidence.summary: nginx config for 8443 deployed; curl to https://$NODE_IP:8443/ returns http_code=200 and openssl s_client confirms cert served with matching dates/serial.
journalctl -t renew-cert shows cron-triggered 'issued new cert' events occurring every ~2 minutes, well before the 5-minute cert lifetime elapses (renewal threshold 180s remaining).

evidence.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests (root cause fix)
evidence.summary: Diagnosed why nginx wasn't reloading (SELinux tmp_t label denial, then cron PATH lacking /usr/sbin for restorecon/nginx); fixed by using absolute paths, confirmed manual run performs full issue+restorecon+nginx -t+reload successfully.

1-second-interval HTTPS polling log shows cert serial transition from ...CF4D (84 consecutive 200s) to ...CF4E (24 consecutive 200s) exactly at the cron-triggered reload, with zero non-200 responses across the whole window.
Captured boot_id 583ddd53-..., uptime -s 2026-09-04 23:36:54, nginx/crond active+enabled, valid cert, HTTPS 200, and recent renewal log entries before rebooting.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot was backgrounded with a 2s delay via nohup so the exec call returned its acknowledgement (PID) before the node dropped off.

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: Connection was lost (confirming the node actually went down) then polled until exec succeeded again; boot_id changed from 583ddd53-... to 3c674d6d-..., and uptime -s advanced to 2026-09-04 23:51:50, proving a genuine reboot rather than a service restart.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services and data on node1
evidence.summary: After reboot, nginx and crond are active, the previously issued cert persisted with correct SELinux cert_t labels, HTTPS answers 200, and the cron renewal schedule file is intact.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart proof that automatic renewal and zero-downtime reload still function
evidence.summary: After reboot, a new cron-triggered renewal fired on schedule (serial ...CF4E -> ...CF4F) with the renew-cert log showing 'issued new cert'/'nginx reloaded', and the 1s-interval HTTPS watch log shows zero non-200 responses across the transition.
